newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania says gold output rose.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania says gold output rose.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Friday it posted record high quarterly gold production for the December quarter following strong performances from its Bounty and Mount McClure gold mines in Western Australia.
The quarter also saw a series of positive exploration results and a further resource upgrade for the Maggie Hays nickel project, also in Western Australia, the company said.

Forrestania announced in November that it has signed an agreement with Normandy Mining Ltd to acquire Normandy's 62 percent interest in Bounty - taking it to 100 percent ownership of the mine, effective November 1.
Attributable share of gold production from both the Bounty and Mount McClure mines totalled 35,474 ounces at an average cash cost of A$400 an ounce, Forrestania said.
The production figure is more than double the result for the previous quarter of 17,624 ounces - which was produced at an average cash cost of A$491 an ounce, Forrestania said.
Gold production for the quarter at Bounty was 31,348 ounces, 32 percent above the previous quarter, while cash operating costs fell to A$418 an ounce from A$536 an ounce.
Cash costs in the month of December were A$393 per ounce for the production of 13,945 ounces, representing the best monthly performance since April, 1994, the company said.

Diamond and in-fill drilling at the Maggie Hays project resulted in the fully diluted resource being upgraded to 17 million tonnes at 1.2 percent nickel at a cut-off of 0.4 percent and 13.4 million tonnes at 1.5 percent nickel at a 0.7 percent nickel cut-off.
The upgrading translates into a a 14 percent increase in contained nickel metal to over 200,000 tonnes, Forrestania said.
The Maggie Hays project is contained within the Lake Johnston joint venture, which is 50 percent owned by Forrestania and 50 percent owned by Gencor Ltd of South Africa.
